messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Depression scores on the HADs improved significantly more with vitamin D3 than with placebo in IBS-D patients.
Sentence: "Symptoms severity, QoL, HADs-depression, and VSI score improved significantly in the vitamin D group as compared to the placebo group (P-values: <0.001, 0.049, 0.023, and 0.008; respectively)."
Measured as: HADs-depression score
Population: Adults aged 18-65 with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome
Intervention: Vitamin D3 50,000 IU/week for 9 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 74
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: After adjustment, vitamin D deficiency was not associated with postpartum depressive symptoms in the whole sample; only anxiety symptoms were associated.
Sentence: "After adjustments for confounders, vitamin D deficiency was only associated with increased postpartum anxiety symptoms ( B = 0.17, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.03-0.30, p = .017) compared to normal vitamin D levels (≥80 nM)."
Measured as: postpartum depressive symptoms (Center for Epidemiologic Studies-Depression)
Population: Women from the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development cohort (n=2483)
Intervention: Early-pregnancy vitamin D status (deficient ≤29.9 nM) measured at median 13 weeks' gestation
Comparator: Normal vitamin D levels (≥80 nM)
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 2,483
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both bear on vitamin D and depressive symptoms, but a 9-week supplementation RCT in IBS-D patients with a positive HADS result conflicts with a cohort finding no association in postpartum women; the deciding difference is who was studied and how vitamin D was assessed.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["design_or_bias","intervention","comparator","outcome_measure"],"detail":"IBS-D adults given 50,000 IU/week for 9 weeks vs postpartum women with early-pregnancy deficiency status (n=2,483 cohort)"}
